### Part A: Importing and Inspecting Data

#A1. Import `employees.csv` into a data frame named `emp_df` using `read.csv()` with `stringsAsFactors = FALSE`.
```{r}
emp_df <- read.csv("employees.csv", stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
```

#A2. Display the structure, the first 5 rows, and summary of `emp_df`.
```{r}
str(emp_df)
head(emp_df, 5)
summary(emp_df)
```

#A3. Print the number of rows and columns of `emp_df`, and the class of every column.
```{r}
nrow(emp_df)
ncol(emp_df)
sapply(emp_df, class)
```

#A4. Print the mean salary, the maximum age, and the number of employees in each department using `table()`.
```{r}
mean(emp_df$salary, na.rm = TRUE)
max(emp_df$age, na.rm = TRUE)
table(emp_df$department)
```

### Part B: Creating Data Frames

#B1. Create a data frame `new_hires` with the same column names as `emp_df`.
```{r}
new_hires <- data.frame(
  emp_id = c(21, 22, 23),
  name = c("Uma", "Victor", "Wen"),
  department = c("HR", "IT", "Sales"),
  sex = c("F", "M", "F"),
  age = c(28, 37, 33),
  salary = c(45000, 83000, 60000),
  years_service = c(2, 9, 6),
  rating = c(3, 4, 5),
  stringsAsFactors = FALSE
)
```

#B2. Use `rbind()` to append `new_hires` to `emp_df`, saving the result as `emp_all`. Print the dimensions of `emp_all`.
```{r}
emp_all <- rbind(emp_df, new_hires)
dim(emp_all)
```

#B3. Add a column `bonus` to `emp_all` equal to 5% of salary, rounded to the nearest whole number.
```{r}
emp_all$bonus <- round(emp_all$salary * 0.05)
```

### Part C: Subsetting

#C1. Extract the first 5 rows and only the columns `name` and `salary`.
```{r}
emp_all[1:5, c("name", "salary")]
```

#C2. Using logical subsetting, select all employees with salary greater than 70000.
```{r}
emp_all[emp_all$salary > 70000, ]
```

#C3. Using `subset()`, select employees in the "IT" department with `years_service` of at least 5.
```{r}
subset(
  emp_all,
  department == "IT" & years_service >= 5,
  select = c(name, years_service, salary)
)
```

#C4. Use `which()` to print the row numbers of employees older than 50, then print their names.
```{r}
over_50 <- which(emp_all$age > 50)
over_50
emp_all$name[over_50]
```

#C5. Remove `emp_id` and `bonus` using negative indexing without overwriting `emp_all`; print the first 3 rows.
```{r}
emp_without_id_bonus <- emp_all[, -which(names(emp_all) %in% c("emp_id", "bonus"))]
head(emp_without_id_bonus, 3)
```

#C6. Using logical indexing, print the salary of the employee whose name is "Mia".
```{r}
emp_all$salary[emp_all$name == "Mia"]
```

### Part D: Factors

#D1. Convert `department` and `sex` in `emp_all` to factors and print `levels()` of each.
```{r}
emp_all$department <- factor(emp_all$department)
emp_all$sex <- factor(emp_all$sex)
levels(emp_all$department)
levels(emp_all$sex)
```

#D2. Use `table()` to count employees per department, and make a two-way table of department by sex.
```{r}
table(emp_all$department)
table(emp_all$department, emp_all$sex)
```

#D3. Create an ordered factor `rating_level` from `rating` and print `table(emp_all$rating_level)`.
```{r}
emp_all$rating_level <- factor(
  emp_all$rating,
  levels = 1:5,
  labels = c("Poor", "Fair", "Good", "Very Good", "Excellent"),
  ordered = TRUE
)
table(emp_all$rating_level)
```

#D4. Using a `for` loop over `levels(emp_all$department)`, print the mean salary of each department, rounded to the nearest whole number.
```{r}
for (dept in levels(emp_all$department)) {
  dept_mean <- mean(emp_all$salary[emp_all$department == dept], na.rm = TRUE)
  print(round(dept_mean))
}
```

### Part E: Conditional Statements

#E1. Using nested `ifelse()`, add `salary_band` and print `table(emp_all$salary_band)`.
```{r}
emp_all$salary_band <- ifelse(
  emp_all$salary >= 70000,
  "High",
  ifelse(emp_all$salary >= 50000, "Medium", "Low")
)
table(emp_all$salary_band)
```

#E2. Using `ifelse()`, add `level` and print `table(emp_all$level)`.
```{r}
emp_all$level <- ifelse(emp_all$years_service >= 8, "Senior", "Junior")
table(emp_all$level)
```

#E3. Write `raise_pct(rating)`, apply it with `sapply()`, compute `new_salary`, and print the first 5 rows.
```{r}
raise_pct <- function(rating) {
  if (rating == 5) {
    return(0.10)
  } else if (rating == 4) {
    return(0.07)
  } else if (rating == 3) {
    return(0.04)
  } else {
    return(0)
  }
}

emp_all$raise <- sapply(emp_all$rating, raise_pct)
emp_all$new_salary <- round(emp_all$salary * (1 + emp_all$raise))
head(emp_all[, c("name", "rating", "raise", "new_salary")], 5)
```

#E4. Compute `total` and check whether it is below 1,600,000 using `if / else`.
```{r}
total <- sum(emp_all$new_salary, na.rm = TRUE)
print(total)

if (total < 1600000) {
  print("Budget OK")
} else {
  print("Over budget")
}
```

### Part F: Sorting

#F1. Use `sort()` to print the 5 highest salary values and the first 5 employee names alphabetically.
```{r}
head(sort(emp_all$salary, decreasing = TRUE), 5)
head(sort(emp_all$name), 5)
```
#F2. Use `order()` to sort `emp_all` by salary descending, save as `by_salary`, and print the top 5.
```{r}
by_salary <- emp_all[order(emp_all$salary, decreasing = TRUE), ]
head(by_salary[, c("name", "department", "salary")], 5)
```
